questions: Did the movements begin suddenly, over hours to a few days?
Does the hand briefly lose its posture or “drop” when you hold the arm out?
Are you fully aware during every episode?
Do the movements occur in the other hand, either leg, or the face?
Do they occur when the affected arm is completely relaxed?
Do they become more pronounced when you hold the arm out or extend the wrist?
Can you temporarily stop them by concentrating or holding the arm with your other hand?
Do they disappear completely during sleep?
Have you recently started, stopped, or increased any medication?
Have you recently taken sedatives, opioid pain medicines, gabapentin, pregabalin, lithium, valproate, phenytoin, or antibiotics?
Have you recently used recreational drugs or had unusually heavy alcohol use or withdrawal?
Do you have known kidney disease?
Do you have known liver disease?
Have you recently had severe vomiting, diarrhea, dehydration, or poor food intake?
Have you recently been unusually sleepy, confused, or less alert?
Have you had shortness of breath or a worsening lung condition recently?
Have you recently had a stroke, head injury, seizure, or loss of consciousness?
Do you have new weakness or numbness on the affected side?
Do you have difficulty speaking, understanding speech, seeing, walking, or maintaining balance?
Do you have neck pain radiating into the affected arm?
Do you have a history of Parkinson’s disease, dystonia, tremor, or other movement disorder?
Do you feel an urge to move the hand or an unpleasant sensation that improves when you move it?
Are the movements rhythmic and regular?
Are they painful?
Have you ever had similar episodes before?
